name: Old Turkic
blurb: Old Turkic was carved in a runic script of its own, read from right to left, on the memorial stones of the Turkic khagans in Mongolia (720s–730s) and on rocks and objects from the Yenisei to the Danube.

scripts.label: Orkhon runes
scripts.about: The runes of the Orkhon inscriptions, raised for Kül Tigin (732) and Bilge Kagan (735) by the Orkhon river in Mongolia, the oldest long texts in a Turkic language.
scripts.note: Type Turkic words as they sound (Tekin’s spelling: ı, ö, ü, q, ɣ or ğ, š, č, ŋ or ng): each consonant takes its back or front form from the word’s vowels, and the vowels are written as on the stones. The keys add one exact sign, back (¹) or front (²). Spaces become the two dots between words.
